newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ends lower.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.

"Treasury bill yields rose slightly today but bond prices ended lower across the board. The interbank rate surged but it did not have an impact on the market. Volume was only moderate with some traders still away on their holidays," a dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.93/1.90 percent compared with Friday's yield of 1.23/1.18 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.33/2.28 percent against 1.73/1.68 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.20/98.25 from Friday's close of S$98.75/98.80, September 2001 at S$97.15/97.20 versus S$97.58/97.63 and June 2003 at S$95.10/95.15 against S$95.58/95.63.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent from Friday's 2-1/2 2-3/8 percent.
